players.product: EPC for data-center campuses (TeraWulf's Kentucky project)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO John Regan: Q2 revenue was $4.3 billion, up 9% from a year ago, on strong execution across the portfolio; adjusted EBITDA was $149 million (vs $96 million a year ago) and adjusted EPS was $0.91 (vs $0.43).
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $4.3 billion (+9%); adjusted EBITDA $149 million (vs $96 million); adjusted EPS $0.91 (vs $0.43)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 new awards were strong at over $6 billion (CEO Jim Breuer: 6.1 in Q2), some of which were not expected until the back half of the year; ending backlog was $26.9 billion after the removal of just over $650 million of backlog of the former Mexico JV. Management now expects a full-year new-awards book-to-bill well above 1 (previously above 1); CEO: Q3/Q4 prospects look very good across LNG, copper and rare earth magnets, including a big data center prospect, though the timing of full releases is hard to predict.
quarterly_data.figure: new awards over $6 billion ($6.1 billion); backlog $26.9 billion; just over $650 million of Mexico JV backlog removed; book-to-bill well above 1

quarterly_data.signal: Revised 2026 guidance (CFO John Regan): adjusted EBITDA $500 million-$525 million (comparable starting point $519 million after about $23 million of foregone second-half profit from the former Mexico JV), implying adjusted EPS of $2.70-$2.80 at the current repurchase tempo; adjusted operating cash flow $300 million-$320 million (a slight raise); new-awards book-to-burn well above one; G&A $170 million-$180 million; tax rate 28%-30%; revenue split about 65% Urban, 20% Energy, 15% Mission with segment margins of 2.5%-3% (Urban), 6%-7% (Energy) and 6% (Mission). The $90 million pre-tax gain on the JV sale is outside the guide.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA $500 million-$525 million; adjusted EPS $2.70-$2.80; adjusted OCF $300 million-$320 million; G&A $170 million-$180 million; tax 28%-30%; margins 2.5%-3% / 6%-7% / 6%

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 segment profit (CFO): Urban Solutions $38 million vs $29 million a year ago, including $44 million of additional losses on the Gordie Howe project (foreign currency, a subcontractor bankruptcy and client-driven changes); Energy Solutions $88 million vs $15 million, largely from higher contributions on projects nearing completion (closeout efforts, in large part already in the original guide); Mission Solutions $44 million vs $35 million on improved fee performance across the DOE portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: Urban $38 million (vs $29 million, incl. $44 million Gordie Howe losses); Energy $88 million (vs $15 million); Mission $44 million (vs $35 million)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 operating cash flow was -$317 million, including a $357 million tax payment associated with the 2025 conversion of Fluor's NuScale shares ($40 million of positive OCF on a more normalized basis without the tax effects); cash was $3 billion at quarter end and back to $3.2 billion at July 31.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 OCF -$317 million (incl. $357 million tax payment); cash $3 billion, $3.2 billion at July 31

quarterly_data.signal: Legacy projects: Fluor completed two legacy infrastructure projects in the quarter (the Gordie Howe International Bridge opened to traffic on July 27; all LBJ main lanes, toll lanes and side roads were turned over to TxDOT) and expects the remaining two (LAX and I-35 Phase 2) to complete by year-end; legacy backlog fell to $120 million. Loss-project funding of $96 million was completed in Q2 and only $94 million of future funding remains, all of which could be concluded in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: legacy backlog $120 million; $96 million funded in Q2; $94 million remaining

quarterly_data.signal: Fluor sold its equity in its Mexican joint venture in July (closed in Q3); management cited diminishing backlog and limited prospects there through the end of the decade, and removed the JV's backlog preemptively in Q2.

Urban Solutions (a majority of revenue) Q2 new awards were $3.2 billion: construction management for a copper mine in Chile, a feasibility study for Anglo's fertilizer project in the U.K., expanded scope on a fertilizer project in Canada, additional scope on a U.S. life sciences project and an infrastructure project in Europe. Prospects include new life sciences work, a rare earth magnet facility, two copper projects in South America and an aluminum rolling mill for an existing Middle East client.

Mining & Metals: clients have signaled more robust capital spending over the next 18 months; Fluor's in-house pipeline holds nearly $30 billion of potential awards (copper, fertilizers, steel and aluminum across South America, North America, Australia, the U.K. and the Middle East). CEO: 'I can't say that all of them are going to go forward, I think a good chunk of them will'; the vast majority of the work is expected to be reimbursable at historic M&M margins.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly $30 billion in-house M&M pipeline (next 18 months)

quarterly_data.signal: Gas-fired power (CEO Jim Breuer): demand for electricity generation, driven by data center growth, industrial expansion and electrification, is creating opportunities in domestic gas-fueled power. Fluor is doing front-end work on an East Coast combined-cycle project, recently submitted a proposal for two single-cycle projects in the Midwest and is advancing a standardized combined-cycle design for a third client; these efforts are expected to support meaningful backlog growth in the first half of 2027. Fluor will not convert to lump sum until it can properly understand and price the risk.

CEO Jim Breuer on the data center ecosystem: 'We see power to be the best play for us in the whole data center ecosystem'; Fluor is working very closely with one client for the data center in Kentucky and looks at the data center market selectively because many projects do not match its selectivity - 'Power, number one. Data centers, number two.'

Nuclear: Fluor booked an award on the Centrus fuel enrichment facility in Q2 (several hundred people working on it, early procurement started; some margin this year, the heavier part next year and beyond); it is progressing FEED work for the X-energy Dow project, preparing a detailed cost estimate for the Cernavoda project in Romania, executing front-end development for a two-reactor expansion at an existing European station and is in discussions with SMR and traditional nuclear technology providers. Fluor has performed design or construction work on 21 nuclear power plants and supported more than 90 reactors with maintenance, outage and operational services; its SMR platforms include NuScale, X-energy and a third technology partner to be unveiled.
quarterly_data.figure: 21 nuclear power plants; more than 90 reactors

quarterly_data.signal: Energy Solutions: Fluor recently signed a long-term agreement with Aramco to support a broad portfolio of capital projects around the globe; Q2 awards included the limited notice to proceed for Phase 2 of the LNG Canada project (client final investment decision expected later this year), a FEED package for a new aromatics facility in Bahrain and a gas compression project for a West Coast client. Fluor is positioning for front-end work in the Canadian oil sands and sees an uptick in domestic front-end refinery work that could become EPC work in 2027 and 2028.

Mission Solutions (Departments of Energy and War): an additional task order to support Operation Epic Fury and extensions of every ongoing intelligence contract this year; Fluor's proposal for the Savannah River rebid (M&O scope combined with the Plutonium Pit project) is in, with a decision anticipated early next year and a six-month extension of current work expected later this year.

CEO Jim Breuer: margins continue to tick up in new awards compared with backlog, with the awards overwhelmingly reimbursable; future lump-sum work in LNG or power is expected to carry higher margins with enough contingency. CFO: the Q2 awards extend meaningfully into 2027 with peak execution in late 2027 and early 2028; in the second half Urban Solutions becomes the larger EBITDA contributor (slight uptick in Urban margins) and a majority of expected second-half EBITDA already sits in backlog.

Middle East (management): Fluor has executed the work in backlog without significant disruption and saw no impact to its guidance directly related to the conflict, while continuing to evaluate implications for clients and its supply chain.

CFO John Regan: Fluor is evaluating inorganic opportunities aligned to its strategic end markets - power, mining, government services (particularly those featuring security clearance) and life sciences / pharma; 'it won't be heavy steel business'.
